coordinates: R=geomspace(10,1500,N) pc; phi=2*pi*(arange(N)*0.6180339887498949 modulo 1); x=R*cos(phi), y=0.8*R*sin(phi). These fixed synthetic evaluation locations do not represent a random scientific sample.
velocity_workload: Fixed v=4*sin(arange(N)*0.71) km/s and e_v=2 km/s, vmem=0. The scalar differentiable workload is the normalized independent Gaussian log likelihood at these positions. No posterior or scientific calibration is inferred from these deterministic velocities.
active_parameters: The first P entries in the ordered params mapping are variables; the remaining physical parameters are fixed constants. P changes the differentiation workload while holding the physical evaluation point and data fixed.

timing.report: Record every duration, median and 10th/90th percentiles. Repeated evaluations of the same input measure steady reuse throughput, not independently recompiled workloads or cold-process latency.
stages: NumPy predictions including per-call native quadrature work
timing.cache_policy: Clear JAX compilation caches between geometry/data-count cases, then keep caches for declared warm repetitions and parameter-count series. All operations use block_until_ready; result host transfer is separately timed.

memory: Record process peak host RSS and externally observed peak device memory. Peaks are high-water marks for a condition, not isolated incremental per-kernel allocations; report their scope.
comparisons: NumPy and JAX axisymmetric predictions use identical quadrature, physical values and points. The spherical NumPy double-exponential and JAX transformed fixed quadratures solve the same physical problem with different numerical rules; require the declared accuracy gate before interpreting timing ratios. No directly differentiable NumPy gradient is claimed. Matched sampler time-to-precision is measured in the separate inference protocol, not extrapolated from this microbenchmark.
stop_rule: Fixed repetitions and orders. Preserve failed accuracy gates, nonfinite values, resource stops and compilation failures. Do not omit a slow case or substitute a tuned numerical rule after seeing timing results.
